# Import necessary modules
import dataclasses
import pathlib

import openpi.models.model as _model
import openpi.transforms as _transforms

from openpi.training.config import DataConfig, DataConfigFactory, ModelTransformFactory
from typing_extensions import override

from rlinf.models.embodiment.openpi.policies import maniskill_policy


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class LeRobotManiSkillDataConfig(DataConfigFactory):
    """
    This config is used to configure transforms that are applied at various parts of the data pipeline.
    For your own dataset, you can copy this class and modify the transforms to match your dataset based on the
    comments below.
    """

    # Flag to enable extra delta action transformation
    extra_delta_transform: bool = False

    @override
    def create(
        self, assets_dirs: pathlib.Path, model_config: _model.BaseModelConfig
    ) -> DataConfig:
        # The repack transform is *only* applied to the data coming from the dataset,
        # and *not* during inference. We can use it to make inputs from the dataset look
        # as close as possible to those coming from the inference environment (e.g. match the keys).
        # Below, we match the keys in the dataset (which we defined in the data conversion script) to
        # the keys we use in our inference pipeline (defined in the inference script for libero).
        # For your own dataset, first figure out what keys your environment passes to the policy server
        # and then modify the mappings below so your dataset's keys get matched to those target keys.
        # The repack transform simply remaps key names here.
        repack_transform = _transforms.Group(
            inputs=[
                _transforms.RepackTransform(
                    {
                        "observation/image": "observation.images.top",
                        "observation/state": "observation.state",
                        "actions": "actions",
                        "prompt": "prompt",  # 'task_descriptions'
                    }
                )
            ]
        )

        # The data transforms are applied to the data coming from the dataset *and* during inference.
        # Below, we define the transforms for data going into the model (``inputs``) and the transforms
        # for data coming out of the model (``outputs``) (the latter is only used during inference).
        # We defined these transforms in `maniskill_policy.py`. You can check the detailed comments there for
        # how to modify the transforms to match your dataset. Once you created your own transforms, you can
        # replace the transforms below with your own.
        data_transforms = _transforms.Group(
            inputs=[
                maniskill_policy.ManiSkillInputs(model_type=model_config.model_type)
            ],
            outputs=[maniskill_policy.ManiSkillOutputs()],
        )

        # One additional data transform: pi0 models are trained on delta actions (relative to the first
        # state in each action chunk). IF your data has ``absolute`` actions (e.g. target joint angles)
        # you can uncomment the following line to convert the actions to delta actions. The only exception
        # is for the gripper actions which are always absolute.
        # In the example below, we would apply the delta conversion to the first 6 actions (joints) and
        # leave the 7th action (gripper) unchanged, i.e. absolute.
        # In Libero, the raw actions in the dataset are already delta actions, so we *do not* need to
        # apply a separate delta conversion (that's why it's commented out). Choose whether to apply this
        # transform based on whether your dataset uses ``absolute`` or ``delta`` actions out of the box.
        # LIBERO already represents actions as deltas,
        # but we have some old Pi0 checkpoints that are trained with this
        # extra delta transform.
        if self.extra_delta_transform:
            delta_action_mask = _transforms.make_bool_mask(6, -1)
            data_transforms = data_transforms.push(
                inputs=[_transforms.DeltaActions(delta_action_mask)],
                outputs=[_transforms.AbsoluteActions(delta_action_mask)],
            )

        # Model transforms include things like tokenizing the prompt and action targets

        model_transforms = ModelTransformFactory()(model_config)

        return dataclasses.replace(
            self.create_base_config(assets_dirs, model_config),
            repack_transforms=repack_transform,
            data_transforms=data_transforms,
            model_transforms=model_transforms,
        )

class HuBERT(Wav2Vec2):
    """
    This lobe enables the integration of HuggingFace and SpeechBrain
    pretrained HuBERT models.
    
    Source paper HuBERT: https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.07447
    
    Transformer from HuggingFace needs to be installed:
    https://huggingface.co/transformers/installation.html
    
    The model can be used as a fixed feature extractor or can be finetuned. It
    will download automatically the model from HuggingFace or use a local path.
    
    For now, HuggingFace's HuBERT and WavLM model can be loaded using the exact code for Wav2Vec2 model.
    For this reason, HuBERT and WavLM can be fine inheriting the Wav2Vec2 class.
    
    Arguments
    ---------
    source : str
        HuggingFace hub name: e.g "facebook/hubert-base-ls960"
    save_path : str
        Path (dir) of the downloaded model.
    output_norm : bool (default: True)
        If True, a layer_norm (affine) will be applied to the output obtained
        from the HuBERT model.
    freeze : bool (default: True)
        If True, the model is frozen. If False, the model will be trained
        alongside with the rest of the pipeline.
    freeze_feature_extractor :  bool (default: False)
        When freeze = False and freeze_feature_extractor True, the feature_extractor module of the model is Frozen. If False
        all the HuBERT model will be trained including feature_extractor module.
    apply_spec_augment : bool (default: False)
        If True, the model will apply spec augment on the output of feature extractor
        (inside huggingface HubertModel() class).
        If False, the model will not apply spec augment. We set this to false to prevent from doing it twice.
    output_all_hiddens : bool (default: False)
        If True, the forward function outputs the hidden states from all transformer layers.
        For example facebook/hubert-base-ls960 has 12 transformer layers and the output is of shape (13, B, T, C),
        where a projection of the CNN output is added to the beginning.
        If False, the forward function outputs the hidden states only from the last transformer layer.
    
    Example
    -------
    >>> import torch
    >>> inputs = torch.rand([10, 600])
    >>> model_hub = "facebook/hubert-base-ls960"
    >>> save_path = "savedir"
    >>> model = HuBERT(model_hub, save_path)
    >>> outputs = model(inputs)
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        source,
        save_path,
        output_norm=False,
        freeze=False,
        freeze_feature_extractor=False,
        apply_spec_augment=False,
        output_all_hiddens=False,
    ):
        # Initialize parent class (Wav2Vec2)
        super().__init__(
            source=source,
            save_path=save_path,
            output_norm=output_norm,
            freeze=freeze,
            freeze_feature_extractor=freeze_feature_extractor,
            apply_spec_augment=apply_spec_augment,
            output_all_hiddens=output_all_hiddens,
        )

# Function to count n-digit numbers starting or ending with 1
def starts_one_ends(n):
    """
    Given a positive integer n, return the count of the numbers of n-digit
    positive integers that start or end with 1.
    """
    # Handle single digit case
    if n == 1:
        return 1
    
    # For n-digit numbers:
    # Numbers starting with 1: 1 * 10^(n-1) choices (1 followed by any n-1 digits)
    # Numbers ending with 1: 9 * 10^(n-2) * 1 choices (first digit 1-9, middle n-2 digits 0-9, last digit 1)
    # Numbers starting AND ending with 1: 1 * 10^(n-2) * 1 choices (overlap to subtract)
    
    # Using inclusion-exclusion principle:
    # |A or B| = |A| + |B| - |A and B|
    
    # Count numbers starting with 1
    starts_with_1 = 10 ** (n - 1)  # 1 followed by any (n-1) digits
    
    # Count numbers ending with 1
    ends_with_1 = 9 * (10 ** (n - 2))  # first digit 1-9, middle (n-2) any, last digit 1
    
    # Count numbers both starting and ending with 1 (to avoid double counting)
    both = 10 ** (n - 2)  # starts with 1 and ends with 1
    
    # Return total count using inclusion-exclusion
    return starts_with_1 + ends_with_1 - both

try:

except ImportError:
    liger_rotary_pos_emb = None


def rotate_half(x):
    """
    Rotates half the hidden dims of the input.
    """
    x1 = x[..., : x.shape[-1] // 2]
    x2 = x[..., x.shape[-1] // 2 :]
    return torch.cat((-x2, x1), dim=-1)


def apply_rotary_pos_emb(q, k, cos, sin, position_ids=None, unsqueeze_dim=2):
    """
    Applies Rotary Position Embedding to the query and key tensors.

    Args:
        q (`torch.Tensor`): The query tensor.
        k (`torch.Tensor`): The key tensor.
        cos (`torch.Tensor`): The cosine part of the rotary embedding.
        sin (`torch.Tensor`): The sine part of the rotary embedding.
        position_ids (`torch.Tensor`, *optional*):
            Deprecated and unused.
        unsqueeze_dim (`int`, *optional*, defaults to 1):
            The 'unsqueeze_dim' argument specifies the dimension along which to unsqueeze 
            cos[position_ids] and sin[position_ids] so that they can be properly broadcasted 
            to the dimensions of q and k. For example, note that cos[position_ids] and 
            sin[position_ids] have the shape [batch_size, seq_len, head_dim]. Then, if q and 
            k have the shape [batch_size, heads, seq_len, head_dim], then setting unsqueeze_dim=1 
            makes cos[position_ids] and sin[position_ids] broadcastable to the shapes of q and k. 
            Similarly, if q and k have the shape [batch_size, seq_len, heads, head_dim], 
            then set unsqueeze_dim=2.

    Returns:
        `tuple(torch.Tensor)` comprising of the query and key tensors rotated using 
        the Rotary Position Embedding.
    """
    cos = cos.unsqueeze(unsqueeze_dim)
    sin = sin.unsqueeze(unsqueeze_dim)
    
    q_embed = (q * cos) + (rotate_half(q) * sin)
    k_embed = (k * cos) + (rotate_half(k) * sin)
    
    return q_embed, k_embed


class RotaryPositionEmbedding(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, use_liger: bool = False):
        super().__init__()
        
        # Handle liger kernel availability
        if use_liger and liger_rotary_pos_emb is None:
            logger.warning(
                "`liger_kernel` is not installed. Will fallback to the default implementation of `apply_rotary_pos_emb`."
            )
            use_liger = False
        
        self.use_liger = use_liger
        self.func = liger_rotary_pos_emb if use_liger else apply_rotary_pos_emb

    def forward(self, q, k, cos, sin, position_ids=None, unsqueeze_dim=2):
        if self.use_liger:
            return liger_rotary_pos_emb(q, k, cos, sin, position_ids, unsqueeze_dim)
        else:
            return apply_rotary_pos_emb(q, k, cos, sin, position_ids, unsqueeze_dim)

    def liger_equivalent(self):
        self.func = (
            liger_rotary_pos_emb
            if liger_rotary_pos_emb is not None
            else apply_rotary_pos_emb
        )
        # Note: this is a module without parameters, so we can return it directly
        return self

from torch import nn

def drop_path(x, drop_prob: float = 0.0, training: bool = False):
    # Return input unchanged if drop_prob is 0 or not in training mode
    if drop_prob == 0.0 or not training:
        return x
    
    # Calculate keep probability
    keep_prob = 1 - drop_prob
    
    # Create shape for random tensor to broadcast across features
    shape = (x.shape[0],) + (1,) * (x.ndim - 1)  # work with diff dim tensors, not just 2D ConvNets
    
    # Generate Bernoulli random tensor
    random_tensor = x.new_empty(shape).bernoulli_(keep_prob)
    
    # Scale the mask if needed
    if keep_prob > 0.0:
        random_tensor.div_(keep_prob)
    
    # Apply dropout mask
    output = x * random_tensor
    return output


class DropPath(nn.Module):
    """Drop paths (Stochastic Depth) per sample (when applied in main path of residual blocks)."""
    
    def __init__(self, drop_prob=None):
        super(DropPath, self).__init__()
        self.drop_prob = drop_prob
    
    def forward(self, x):
        return drop_path(x, self.drop_prob, self.training)

from typing import List, Optional
from enum import Enum

# Define dimension types as an enumeration
class DimensionType(str, Enum):
    APPLICATION = "application_first"
    INFRASTRUCTURE = "infrastructure_first"
    INSTANCE = "instance_first"
    CUSTOM = "custom"

# Dimension resolver class for handling dimension strategies
class DimensionResolver:
    # Predefined dimension mappings for each type
    PRESET_DIMENSION_MAP = {
        DimensionType.APPLICATION: ["service"],
        DimensionType.INFRASTRUCTURE: ["location"],
        DimensionType.INSTANCE: ["resource_name"],
    }
    
    # Fallback order for dimension resolution
    FALLBACK_ORDER = [
        DimensionType.APPLICATION,
        DimensionType.INFRASTRUCTURE,
        DimensionType.INSTANCE,
    ]
    
    @classmethod
    def resolve_dimensions_for_strategy(
        cls,
        dimension_type: str,
        custom_dimensions: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    ) -> List[List[str]]:
        # Handle custom dimension type
        if dimension_type == DimensionType.CUSTOM.value or dimension_type == "custom":
            if custom_dimensions:
                return [custom_dimensions]
            return [["event_id"]]
        
        try:
            # Convert string to DimensionType enum
            dim_type = DimensionType(dimension_type)
        except ValueError:
            # Default to INSTANCE on invalid input
            dim_type = DimensionType.INSTANCE
        
        # Find starting index in fallback order
        start_index = cls.FALLBACK_ORDER.index(dim_type)
        result = []
        
        # Build result by iterating through fallback types
        for fallback_type in cls.FALLBACK_ORDER[start_index:]:
            result.append(cls.PRESET_DIMENSION_MAP[fallback_type])
        
        # Always append event_id as final fallback
        result.append(["event_id"])
        return result

class DualStackServer(socketserver.TCPServer):
    """Listens on both IPv4 and IPv6 loopback so ``localhost`` works on Windows
    regardless of whether the browser resolves it to 127.0.0.1 or ::1."""
    allow_reuse_address = True

    def server_bind(self):
        try:
            self.socket = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET6, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
            self.socket.setsockopt(socket.IPPROTO_IPV6, socket.IPV6_V6ONLY, 0)
            self.socket.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
            self.socket.bind(("::", self.server_address[1], 0, 0))
        except (OSError, AttributeError):
            # Fall back to plain IPv4 if dual-stack is unavailable
            self.socket = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
            self.socket.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
            self.socket.bind(("0.0.0.0", self.server_address[1]))
        self.server_address = self.socket.getsockname()


# Start the server

def is_within_directory(base_dir: str, target: str) -> bool:
    """
    Return True if the target path is within the given base directory.
    """
    # Resolve both paths to absolute form
    base_path = Path(base_dir).resolve()
    target_path = Path(target).resolve()

    # Handle Windows-specific path normalization
    if os.name == "nt":
        base_norm = os.path.normcase(os.path.normpath(str(base_path)))
        target_norm = os.path.normcase(os.path.normpath(str(target_path)))

        try:
            return os.path.commonpath([target_norm, base_norm]) == base_norm
        except ValueError:
            return False

    # For Python >= 3.9, use is_relative_to
    try:
        return target_path.is_relative_to(base_path)
    except AttributeError:  # Fallback for Python < 3.9
        try:
            return os.path.commonpath([target_path, base_path]) == str(base_path)
        except ValueError:
            return False


def normalize_path_for_match(path: str) -> str:
    """
    Normalize a path string for safe, cross-platform prefix comparisons.
    """
    # Replace backslashes with forward slashes
    normalized = path.replace("\\", "/")
    # Collapse multiple slashes into one
    normalized = re.sub(r"/+", "/", normalized)

    # Handle Windows UNC-style paths (e.g., /?/C:/...)
    if normalized.startswith("/?/"):
        normalized = normalized[3:]

    # Strip trailing slash and convert to lowercase
    return normalized.rstrip("/").lower()


def is_absolute_archive_path(path: str) -> bool:
    """
    Return True if the path is absolute in a platform-agnostic archive context.
    """
    # Normalize separators
    normalized = path.replace("\\", "/")

    # Check for Unix-style absolute path or Windows drive letter
    return normalized.startswith("/") or bool(re.match(r"^[a-zA-Z]:", normalized))


def is_critical_system_path(path: str, critical_paths: Iterable[str]) -> bool:
    """
    Return True if path targets a critical system location (normalized match).
    """
    normalized_path = normalize_path_for_match(path)

    for critical in critical_paths:
        normalized_critical = normalize_path_for_match(critical)

        # Exact match or prefix match with slash separator
        if normalized_path == normalized_critical or normalized_path.startswith(f"{normalized_critical}/"):
            return True

    return False


def sanitize_archive_path(entry_name: str, base_dir: str) -> tuple[str, bool]:
    """
    Return normalized path for archive entry and whether it stays within base.

    Parameters
    ----------
    entry_name: str
        Name of the entry in the archive.
    base_dir: str
        Intended extraction directory used for normalization.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[str, bool]
        (resolved_path, is_safe) where ``is_safe`` is ``False`` if the entry
        would escape ``base_dir`` when extracted.
    """
    base_path = Path(base_dir).resolve()

    # Normalize path separators
    entry = entry_name.replace("\\", "/")

    # Reject absolute paths (Unix-style or Windows drive-letter style)
    if entry.startswith("/") or (len(entry) > 1 and entry[1] == ":"):
        resolved = (base_path / entry.lstrip("/")).resolve()
        return str(resolved), False

    # Remove leading slashes
    entry = entry.lstrip("/")

    # Resolve full path
    resolved = (base_path / entry).resolve()

    # Determine safety using appropriate method based on Python version
    try:
        is_safe = resolved.is_relative_to(base_path)
    except AttributeError:  # Python < 3.9
        try:
            is_safe = os.path.commonpath([resolved, base_path]) == str(base_path)
        except ValueError:  # Windows: different drives
            is_safe = False

    return str(resolved), is_safe

import jax
import jax.numpy as np
import parametricmatrixmodels as pmm

def test_treeflatten():
    r"""
    Test the TreeFlatten module
    """
    # Set up parameters
    batch_dim = 10
    key = jax.random.key(0)
    
    # Create test data
    arr = jax.random.normal(key, (batch_dim, 3, 4))
    data = ({"a": arr, "b": {"c": arr, "d": [arr, arr]}},)
    
    # Initialize and compile the TreeFlatten module
    tree_flatten = pmm.modules.TreeFlatten()
    tree_flatten.compile(key, jax.tree.map(lambda x: x.shape[1:], data))
    
    # Run the forward pass
    out, _ = tree_flatten(data)
    
    # Verify output structure and values
    expected_out = jax.tree.leaves(data)
    expected_struct = jax.tree.structure(expected_out)
    out_struct = jax.tree.structure(out)
    
    assert expected_struct == out_struct
    
    for expected, actual in zip(expected_out, out):
        assert np.allclose(expected, actual)

# Simple model definition
class SimpleModel(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.fc1 = nn.Linear(900, 256)
        self.fc2 = nn.Linear(256, 256)
        self.fc3 = nn.Linear(256, 900 * 12)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        x = torch.relu(self.fc1(x))
        x = torch.relu(self.fc2(x))
        return self.fc3(x).view(-1, 900, 12)

# Create model and move to device
model = SimpleModel().to(device)
print(f"Model on device: {next(model.parameters()).device}")
print(f"Model parameters: {sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())/1e6:.1f}M")

# Create dummy data
batch_size = 16

dummy_target = torch.randint(0, 12, (batch_size, 900)).to(device)

# Setup training components

optimizer = optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.001)

# Training loop
print("\nStarting training loop...")

    start = time.time()
    
    optimizer.zero_grad()
    output = model(dummy_input)
    loss = criterion(output.transpose(1, 2), dummy_target)
    loss.backward()
    optimizer.step()
    
    elapsed = time.time() - start
    print(f"Epoch {epoch}: Loss={loss.item():.4f}, Time={elapsed:.3f}s")

# Function to compute rounded average and convert to binary
def rounded_avg(n, m):
    """You are given two positive integers n and m, and your task is to compute the
    average of the integers from n through m (including n and m). 
    Round the answer to the nearest integer and convert that to binary.
    If n is greater than m, return -1.
    Example:
    rounded_avg(1, 5) => "0b11"
    rounded_avg(7, 5) => -1
    rounded_avg(10, 20) => "0b1111"
    rounded_avg(20, 33) => "0b11010"
    """
    # Check if n is greater than m
    if n > m:
        return -1
    
    # Calculate count of numbers in range
    count = m - n + 1
    
    # Calculate total sum using arithmetic series formula
    total = count * (n + m) // 2
    
    # Compute average and round to nearest integer
    avg = round(total / count)
    
    # Convert to binary representation
    return bin(avg)

# Function to download word lists from a URL
def download_word_lists(base_url: str, file_names: Union[str, list], request_headers: dict = {}, 
                        file_extensions: list = [], save_path: str = "") -> None:
    """
    Downloads specified word list files from a given URL and saves them in a designated directory.
    
    Args:
        base_url (str): The base URL where the word lists are hosted.
        file_names (Union[str, list]): Name(s) of the word list file(s) to download. Can be a single string or a list of strings.
        request_headers (dict): Optional HTTP headers to include in the requests.
        file_extensions (list): List of allowed file extensions; only matching files will be saved.
        save_path (str): Directory path where downloaded files will be stored.
        
    Returns:
        None
    """
    # Create the directory if it doesn't exist
    if not os.path.isdir(save_path):
        os.makedirs(save_path)

            if file_extensions:

                    if filename.endswith(ext):
                        output_path = os.path.join(save_path, filename)
                        with open(output_path, 'wb') as f:

                        break  # Exit extension loop after successful match/write

                # Save file without extension filtering
                output_path = os.path.join(save_path, filename)

# Process and resize image with optional channel selection and dtype conversion
import numpy as np
import cv2
from typing import Tuple

def process_image(img: np.ndarray, factor: Tuple[float, float]) -> np.ndarray:
    # Limit to first three channels if more than 3 exist
    if len(img.shape) > 2 and img.shape[2] > 3:
        img = img[:, :, :3]
    
    # Apply resizing if scale factors differ from (1.0, 1.0)
    if factor != (1.0, 1.0):
        w = img.shape[1]
        h = img.shape[0]
        img = cv2.resize(img, (int(factor[0] * w), int(factor[1] * h)), interpolation=cv2.INTER_NEAREST)
    
    # Convert data type if necessary
    if img.dtype == np.float64:
        img = img.astype(np.float32)
        
    return img

# Process dynamic spectrum data with RFI masking and binning
def handle_dynamic_spectrum(spectrum, spectrumP, config_params):
    # Apply RFI masking on pixels and channels before binning; pixels again after binning for LS band
    spectrum.flag_RFI_pixels(sigma_factor=config_params['pixflag_sigfacLS'], operation=imag)
    spectrum.flag_RFI(sigma_factor=config_params['chanflag_sigfacLS'])
    nt_ls = int(round(config_params['tint_LS'] / spectrum.dt()))  # integrations to combine for LS band
    nf_ls = int(round(config_params['df_MHz_LS'] / (spectrum.df() / 1e6)))  # channels to combine for LS band
    spectrum = spectrum.combine_dynspec(time_bins=nt_ls, freq_bins=nf_ls, partial_masking=config_params['maskpartial_LS'])
    spectrum.flag_RFI_pixels(sigma_factor=config_params['pixflag_sigfacLS'], operation=imag)  # Re-mask pixels after binning for LS band
    
    if spectrumP:
        # Apply RFI masking on pixels and channels before binning for P band
        spectrumP.flag_RFI_pixels(sigma_factor=config_params['pixflag_sigfacP'])
        spectrumP.flag_RFI(sigma_factor=config_params['chanflag_sigfacP'])
        nt_p = int(round(config_params['tint_P'] / spectrumP.dt()))  # integrations to combine for P band
        nf_p = int(round(config_params['df_MHz_P'] / (spectrumP.df() / 1e6)))  # channels to combine for P band
        spectrumP = spectrumP.combine_dynspec(time_bins=nt_p, freq_bins=nf_p, partial_masking=False)  # mask_partial always False for P band
    
    return spectrum, spectrumP

# Convert polar coordinates to Cartesian coordinates
import numpy as np

def polar_to_cartesian(polar_coords, mesh_points):
    """
    Transform polar coordinates into Cartesian coordinates.
    
    Parameters
    ----------
    polar_coords : ndarray
        Array of polar coordinates with shape (Nnodes, Ndof)
    mesh_points : ndarray
        Array of points in the mesh
        
    Returns
    -------
    cartesian_coords : ndarray
        Array of Cartesian coordinates with shape (Nnodes, Ndof)
    """
    radius = polar_coords[:, 0]  # Extracting radial distance from polar coordinates
    angle = polar_coords[:, 1]   # Extracting angular coordinate from polar coordinates
    x_coord = radius * np.cos(angle)  # Calculating x coordinate in Cartesian system
    y_coord = radius * np.sin(angle)  # Calculating y coordinate in Cartesian system
    cartesian_coords = np.column_stack((x_coord, y_coord))  # Combining x and y coordinates into cartesian_coords
    return cartesian_coords

# Extract file information based on patterns in content and filename
import glob
import re

def extract_file_info(pattern):
    results = []
    rss_pattern = re.compile(r'kb=(\d+)')
    size_pattern = re.compile(r'size=(\d+)')
    
    for filepath in glob.iglob(pattern):
        with open(filepath) as file:
            first_line = file.readline()
            kb_match = rss_pattern.search(first_line)
            size_match = size_pattern.search(filepath)
            
            if kb_match and size_match:
                kb_value = int(kb_match.group(1))
                size_value = int(size_match.group(1))
                results.append({
                    'path': filepath,
                    'kb': kb_value,
                    'size': size_value
                })
                
    return results

# A simple 64-bit set implementation using XOR obfuscation
class SimpleSet64:
    def __init__(self, initial_value: int):
        self.seed = initial_value
        self.data = set()
    
    def insert(self, item: int) -> None:
        self.data.add(item ^ self.seed)
    
    def erase(self, item: int) -> None:
        self.data.discard(item ^ self.seed)
    
    def has(self, item: int) -> bool:
        return (item ^ self.seed) in self.data
    
    def reset(self) -> None:
        self.data.clear()

# Verification tests
def verify_simple_set64():
    seed_value = 54321
    test_set = SimpleSet64(seed_value)
    
    # Verify insertion and membership checks
    test_set.insert(100)
    test_set.insert(200)
    assert test_set.has(100) is True
    assert test_set.has(200) is True
    assert test_set.has(300) is False
    
    # Verify deletion functionality
    test_set.erase(100)
    assert test_set.has(100) is False
    
    # Verify clearing all elements
    test_set.reset()
    assert test_set.has(200) is False
    assert test_set.has(300) is False

verify_simple_set64()

def store_proxy(server_host, server_port):
    # Open the proxy database in create/write mode
    with gdbm.open("proxydb", "c") as database:
        # Store the server address and port as encoded bytes
        database[server_host.encode()] = str(server_port).encode()

def retrieve_proxy(server_host):
    # Open the proxy database in read mode
    with gdbm.open("proxydb", "r") as database:
        # Retrieve the port for the given server address
        port_data = database.get(server_host.encode())
        # Convert to integer if found, otherwise return None
        return int(port_data) if port_data else None

def remove_proxy(server_host):
    # Open the proxy database in write mode
    with gdbm.open("proxydb", "w") as database:
        # Check if the server address exists before deletion
        if server_host.encode() in database:
            del database[server_host.encode()]

# Train a Hierarchical Recurrent Encoder-Decoder (HRED) model
import torch
from argparse import ArgumentParser
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader
from hred_dataset import HREDDataset  # Custom dataset for HRED architecture

def execute_training(args):
    # Prepare data loader
    training_set = HREDDataset(...)  # Instantiate dataset with required arguments
    train_loader = DataLoader(training_set, batch_size=args.batch_size, shuffle=True)
    
    # Initialize HRED model and move to appropriate device
    hred_network = HREDModel(...)  # Configure model with suitable hyperparameters
    hred_network.to(device)
    
    # Set up optimizer and loss function
    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(hred_network.parameters(), lr=args.learning_rate)
    loss_fn = torch.nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
    
    # Main training loop
    for ep in range(args.epochs):
        for step, (features, labels) in enumerate(train_loader):
            features, labels = features.to(device), labels.to(device)
            
            # Compute predictions
            predictions = hred_network(features)
            
            # Calculate loss
            current_loss = loss_fn(predictions, labels)
            
            # Update weights
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            current_loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
            
            # Periodic logging
            if step % args.logging_interval == 0:
                print(f'Epoch [{ep+1}/{args.epochs}], Step [{step+1}/{len(train_loader)}], Loss: {current_loss.item()}')
        
        # Save model checkpoint periodically
        if (ep + 1) % args.checkpoint_interval == 0:
            torch.save(hred_network.state_dict(), f'model_epoch_{ep+1}.pt')
    
    print('Training finished successfully.')

import re

def clean_and_limit_title(title):
    """
    Cleans the provided title by stripping out non-alphanumeric characters,
    transforming it to lowercase, and limiting its length to 64 characters.
    
    Args:
    title (str): The original title to be processed.
    
    Returns:
    str: The cleaned and limited title.
    """
    # Compile regex pattern to match non-alphanumeric characters (including underscores)
    special_chars = re.compile(r'[\W_]+')
    
    # Handle empty or None input
    if not title:
        return ""
    
    # Remove special characters and convert to lowercase
    cleaned = special_chars.sub("", title)
    cleaned = cleaned.lower()
    
    # Truncate if exceeds maximum length
    if len(cleaned) > 64:
        return cleaned[:64]
    
    return cleaned

    def begin_client_processing(self):

    def end_client_processing(self):
        # Terminate client event processing
        self.client_processing_active = False
        
    def shutdown(self):
        if self.receiving_active:
            self.end_receiving()
        if self.client_processing_active:

# Compute the average excluding the smallest and largest values
from typing import List

def compute_trimmed_average(values: List[float]) -> float:
    if len(values) < 3:
        raise ValueError("Input list must contain at least 3 elements")
    
    lowest = min(values)
    highest = max(values)
    
    adjusted_sum = sum(values) - lowest - highest
    adjusted_count = len(values) - 2  # Remove min and max
    
    return adjusted_sum / adjusted_count

def check_against_minimum_limit(input_value, min_limit):
    """
    Determine whether the input value is at least as large as the specified minimum limit.
    Args:
    input_value: The numeric value to evaluate.
    min_limit: The minimum acceptable threshold for comparison.
    Returns:
    True if input_value is greater than or equal to min_limit, False otherwise.

import numpy as np
def process_missing_data(target, features=None):
    """
    Process missing values in the input arrays.
    Parameters:
    target : array-like or None, shape=(n_samples,)
        The dependent (time-series) array.
    features : array-like or None, shape=(n_samples, n_features), optional
        The independent (feature) array.
    Returns:
    target_processed : array-like, shape=(n_samples,)
        The dependent array with missing values addressed.
    features_processed : array-like, shape=(n_samples, n_features)
        The independent array with missing values addressed, if features is not None.
    """
    if features is not None:
        # Address missing values in both target and features
        target_processed = np.nan_to_num(target)
        features_processed = np.nan_to_num(features)
    else:
        # Address missing values in target only
        target_processed = np.nan_to_num(target)
        features_processed = None
    return target_processed, features_processed

        if term in self.keyword_store:

        else:
            self.keyword_store[term] = description

        if term in self.keyword_store:
            self.current_keyword = term
        else:

        """
        Create a summary of all keywords and their descriptions.
        """
        summary = "Keyword Summary:\n"
        for term, description in self.keyword_store.items():
            status_marker = " (Active)" if term == self.current_keyword else ""
            summary += f"{term}: {description}{status_marker}\n"

# Verify a signed blob using GPG
from typing import Optional
from pathlib import Path
import gnupg

def checkBlobSignature(signedContent: bytes, sigData: bytes, *, keyId: str = None, keyPath: Path = None, subKeyId: str = None) -> bool:
    gpg_instance = gnupg.GPG()
    
    if keyPath:
        with open(keyPath, 'rb') as key_file:
            imported_key_result = gpg_instance.import_keys(key_file.read())
            if not imported_key_result.results:
                raise ValueError("Unable to import the provided key file")
    
    if keyId:
        gpg_instance.recv_keys('keyserver.ubuntu.com', keyId)
    
    if subKeyId:
        gpg_instance.recv_keys('keyserver.ubuntu.com', subKeyId)
    
    verification_result = gpg_instance.verify(signedContent, sigData)
    
    return verification_result.valid

import urllib
import re

def get_open_price(stock_symbol):
    # Construct the finance URL for the given stock symbol
    base_url = 'http://finance.google.com/finance?q=' + stock_symbol
    # Read the content from the URL
    page_content = urllib.urlopen(base_url).read()
    # Search for the opening price using regex
    match = re.search('".*?op".*?>(.*?)<', page_content)
    # Extract matched value or return 'N/A' if not found
    open_price = match.group(1) if match else 'N/A'
    return open_price

    # Construct the finance URL for the given stock symbol
    base_url = 'http://finance.google.com/finance?q=' + stock_symbol
    # Read the content from the URL
    page_content = urllib.urlopen(base_url).read()
    # Search for the high price using regex
    match = re.search('".*?hi".*?>(.*?)<', page_content)
    # Extract matched value or return 'N/A' if not found

# Convert a gzipped file to a plain text file with UTF-8 encoding
def compress_to_text(compressed_path, output_path):
    """
    Decompress a .gz file and save its content as a UTF-8 encoded text file.
    compressed_path: path to the input gzipped file
    output_path: path where the decompressed text file will be saved
    """
    import gzip
    with gzip.open(compressed_path, 'rb') as source_file:
        with open(output_path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as target_file:
            target_file.write(source_file.read().decode('utf-8'))

def custom_random_interval(min_val, max_val=None, shape=None):
    """
    Generate a uniform float random number between min_val and max_val.
    
    Args:
    min_val (float): The lower bound of the range for generating random numbers.
    max_val (float, optional): The upper bound of the range for generating random numbers. If not provided, it defaults to None.
    shape (int or tuple of ints, optional): The shape of the output array. If not provided, it defaults to None.

    """
    if max_val is None:
        min_val, max_val = 0, min_val

import asyncio

class JobController:
    def __init__(self):
        self._event_loop = asyncio.get_event_loop()
        self._lock_mutex = asyncio.Lock()
        self._not_full_condition = asyncio.Condition(lock=self._lock_mutex)
        self._active_tasks = set()
    
    async def _signal_not_full(self) -> None:
        async def trigger() -> None:
            async with self._lock_mutex:
                self._not_full_condition.notify()
        
        task = self._event_loop.run_in_executor(None, trigger)
        task.add_done_callback(self._active_tasks.discard)
        self._active_tasks.add(task)

from contextlib import contextmanager
from .file import H5File

@contextmanager
def open_hdf5_file(filepath, access_mode='r', **options):
    """Context manager for reading and writing an HDF5 file as an H5File object.
    
    Parameters
    ----------
    filepath : str
        The name of the HDF5 file to open.
    access_mode : str, optional
        The file access mode ('r', 'r+', 'w', 'a', etc.), by default 'r'.
    **options
        Additional keyword arguments to be passed to the H5File constructor.
        
    Yields
    ------
    H5File
        An H5File object for interacting with the HDF5 file.
        
    Raises
    ------
    IOError
        If the file cannot be opened or created.
    """
    file_handle = None
    try:
        file_handle = H5File(filepath, access_mode, **options)
        yield file_handle
    except Exception as error:
        if file_handle is not None:
            file_handle.close()
        raise error
    finally:
        if file_handle is not None:
            file_handle.close()

import random
from PIL import Image

class RandomFlip(CustomTransform):
    def __init__(self, horizontal_prob=0, vertical_prob=0):
        """
        Arguments:
        ----------
        horizontal_prob: range [0, 1], probability to apply horizontal flip, setting to 0 disables this operation
        vertical_prob: range [0, 1], probability to apply vertical flip
        """
        self.horizontal_prob = horizontal_prob
        self.vertical_prob = vertical_prob
        
    def __call__(self, image_data):
        """
        Apply random horizontal and vertical flips to the input image based on specified probabilities.
        Arguments:
        ----------
        image_data: input image to be transformed
        Returns:
        --------
        augmented_image: image after applying random flips
        """
        # Convert input to PIL Image if needed
        if not isinstance(image_data, Image.Image):
            image_data = Image.fromarray(image_data)
            
        # Apply horizontal flip with probability horizontal_prob
        if random.random() < self.horizontal_prob:
            image_data = image_data.transpose(Image.FLIP_LEFT_RIGHT)
            
        # Apply vertical flip with probability vertical_prob
        if random.random() < self.vertical_prob:
            image_data = image_data.transpose(Image.FLIP_TOP_BOTTOM)
            
        return image_data

# Calculate distances between consecutive points and angles of the polygon
import math

def segment_lengths(coords):
    return [math.sqrt((coords[j][0] - coords[j+1][0])**2 + (coords[j][1] - coords[j+1][1])**2) for j in range(len(coords)-1)]

def interior_angles(coords):
    angle_list = []
    for idx in range(len(coords)):
        pt_prev = coords[idx-1]
        pt_curr = coords[idx]
        pt_next = coords[(idx+1) % len(coords)]
        
        vec1 = (pt_prev[0] - pt_curr[0], pt_prev[1] - pt_curr[1])
        vec2 = (pt_next[0] - pt_curr[0], pt_next[1] - pt_curr[1])
        
        dot_val = vec1[0]*vec2[0] + vec1[1]*vec2[1]
        len_vec1 = math.sqrt(vec1[0]**2 + vec1[1]**2)
        len_vec2 = math.sqrt(vec2[0]**2 + vec2[1]**2)
        
        angle_measure = math.acos(dot_val / (len_vec1 * len_vec2))
        angle_list.append(angle_measure)
    
    return angle_list

def is_square_like(coord_list, tolerance=0.6) -> bool:
    seg_lengths = segment_lengths(coord_list)
    min_len = float(min(seg_lengths))
    max_len = float(max(seg_lengths))
    length_ratio = min_len / max_len
    
    lengths_acceptable = length_ratio >= tolerance
    angles_acceptable = all(abs(a - interior_angles(coord_list)[0]) < 0.1 for a in interior_angles(coord_list))
    
    return lengths_acceptable and angles_acceptable

# Calculate projected context for attention mechanism
import numpy as np
import theano.tensor as T

def compute_attention_projection(context, parameters, layer_prefix, attention_mask=None, hidden_init=None):
    """
    Compute the projected context used in attention-based neural network models.
    
    Args:
    - context: 3D tensor of shape (#annotation x #sample x dim) representing input annotations
    - parameters: Dictionary containing shared variables for model parameters
    - layer_prefix: String prefix for parameter naming convention
    - attention_mask: Optional 2D mask tensor with shape (input_seq_len x 1)
    - hidden_init: Optional initial hidden state with shape (batch_size x dim)
    
    Returns:
    - projected_context: 3D tensor of shape (#annotation x #sample x dim) after linear projection
    """
    # Handle missing mask by creating ones tensor
    if attention_mask is None:
        attention_mask = T.alloc(1., context.shape[0], 1)
    
    # Determine dimension from parameter matrix
    hidden_dim = parameters[prfx(layer_prefix, 'Wcx')].shape[1]
    
    # Initialize hidden state if not provided
    if hidden_init is None:
        hidden_init = T.alloc(0., context.shape[1], hidden_dim)
    
    # Validate input dimensions
    assert context.ndim == 3, 'Context must be 3-dimensional: #annotation x #sample x dim'
    
    # Apply linear transformation to context
    projected_context = T.dot(context, parameters[prfx(layer_prefix, 'Wc_att')]) + parameters[prfx(layer_prefix, 'b_att')]
    
    return projected_context

# Database management module using SQLite
import sqlite3

class SettingsHandler:
    def __init__(self, database_path):
        self.connection = sqlite3.connect(database_path)
        self.cursor = self.connection.cursor()
        self.initialize_settings_table()
    
    def initialize_settings_table(self):
        create_sql = """
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS settings (
                setting_key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                setting_value TEXT
            )
        """
        self.cursor.execute(create_sql)
        self.connection.commit()
    
    def add_setting(self, pair):
        insert_sql = """
            INSERT INTO settings (setting_key, setting_value) VALUES(?, ?)
        """
        self.cursor.execute(insert_sql, pair)
        self.connection.commit()
    
    def modify_setting(self, pair):
        update_sql = """
            UPDATE settings SET setting_value=? WHERE setting_key=?
        """
        self.cursor.execute(update_sql, pair)
        self.connection.commit()
    
    def disconnect(self):
        self.connection.close()

def run():

    handler.add_setting(('appearance', 'dark'))
    handler.add_setting(('text_size', '14'))
    handler.modify_setting(('text_size', '16'))
    handler.disconnect()

# Plot buffered geometries from a GeoDataFrame on a map using Holoviews and Geoviews
import geopandas as gpd
import holoviews as hv
import geoviews as gv

def visualize_buffered_features(geo_df, buffer_radius, *params, **options):
    """
    Visualize buffered geometries from a GeoDataFrame on an interactive map.
    
    Parameters:
    -----------
    geo_df : geopandas.GeoDataFrame
        GeoDataFrame containing geometries to be buffered.
    buffer_radius : numeric
        Size of the buffer in meters (measured in EPSG:31287).
    *params, **options : additional arguments and keyword arguments
        Additional arguments and keyword arguments to be passed to the plotting functions.
        
    Returns:
    --------
    hv.Layout
        Plot of the buffered geometries overlaid on a map.
        
    Raises:
    -------
    ValueError
        If the input GeoDataFrame is empty or does not contain valid geometries.
    """
    if geo_df.empty or geo_df.geometry.isna().all():
        raise ValueError("Input GeoDataFrame is empty or does not contain valid geometries.")
    
    # Reproject to EPSG:31287 CRS and apply buffer operation
    buffered_geoms = geo_df.to_crs('epsg:31287').buffer(buffer_radius)
    
    # Create new GeoDataFrame with buffered geometries and reproject to EPSG:4326
    buffered_layer = geo_df.copy().set_geometry(buffered_geoms).to_crs('epsg:4326')
    
    # Generate visualization: buffered areas (semi-transparent) overlaid on original features
    visualization = (buffered_layer.hvplot(geo=True, tiles='OSM', alpha=0.4, line_width=1, *params, **options) *
                     geo_df.hvplot(geo=True, hover_cols=['DESIGNATION'])
                    ).opts(active_tools=['wheel_zoom'])
    
    return visualization

# Generate a boolean mask for sequences based on their lengths
def create_sequence_mask(seq_lengths, max_length=None):
    """
    Generates a boolean mask indicating valid positions in sequences.
    
    Args:
    seq_lengths (list): A list containing the lengths of each sequence.
    max_length (int, optional): The maximum sequence length to consider. Defaults to None.
    
    Returns:
    list: A boolean mask where True indicates valid positions and False indicates padding.
    """
    if max_length is None:
        max_length = max(seq_lengths)  # Determine the maximum length from the input if not specified
    
    mask = [pos < seq_len for seq_len in seq_lengths for pos in range(max_length)]  # Construct boolean mask based on sequence lengths
    
    return mask

# Encrypt a configuration file using AES in CBC mode
import argparse
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import padding
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.ciphers import Cipher, algorithms, modes
from cryptography.hazmat.backends import default_backend

def secure_config_file(output_path, encryption_key, initialization_vector):
    try:
        with open('config_file.txt', 'rb') as input_file:
            plaintext_data = input_file.read()
        
        backend = default_backend()
        cipher = Cipher(algorithms.AES(encryption_key), modes.CBC(initialization_vector), backend=backend)
        encryptor = cipher.encryptor()
        
        padder = padding.PKCS7(128).padder()
        padded_plaintext = padder.update(plaintext_data) + padder.finalize()
        ciphertext = encryptor.update(padded_plaintext) + encryptor.finalize()
        
        with open(output_path, 'wb') as result_file:
            result_file.write(ciphertext)
        print("Configuration file encrypted and saved to", output_path)
    
    except FileNotFoundError:
        print("Error: Configuration file not found")
    except ValueError:
        print("Error: Invalid key or initialization vector")
    except Exception as error:
        print("An error occurred:", str(error))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='Encrypt configuration file using AES-CBC encryption')
    parser.add_argument('output_file', type=argparse.FileType('wb'),
                        help='Output binary file, e.g. encrypted_config.bin')
    parser.add_argument('--encryption-key', type=lambda x: x.encode(), default=b'',
                        help="AES encryption key (must be 16, 24, or 32 bytes)")
    parser.add_argument('--iv', type=str, default='',
                        help="Initialization vector for CBC mode (digimobil routers)")
    arguments = parser.parse_args()
    secure_config_file(arguments.output_file.name, arguments.encryption_key, arguments.iv)

# Asynchronous HTTP client session wrapper using aiohttp
import aiohttp
import asyncio
from typing import Optional

class AsyncHttpClient:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._client_session: Optional[aiohttp.ClientSession] = None
    
    async def fetch_url(self, endpoint: str) -> str:
        if self._client_session is None:
            self._client_session = aiohttp.ClientSession()
        try:
            async with self._client_session.get(endpoint) as resp:
                return await resp.text()
        except aiohttp.ClientError as err:
            return f"Failed to retrieve {endpoint}: {err}"
        finally:
            if self._client_session is not None:
                await self._client_session.close()

class RestrictiveMethodMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware):
    async def dispatch(self, request: Request, call_next):
        # Only allow safe HTTP methods

# Fire detection system using Kafka messaging
from kafka import KafkaProducer
import time

def handle_temp_reading(data: bytes, target_topic: str) -> None:
    # Initialize Kafka producer connection
    kafka_client = KafkaProducer(bootstrap_servers=['localhost:9092'])
    
    # Decode and parse the incoming message
    raw_data = data.decode('utf-8')
    parts = raw_data.split(' ')
    
    # Extract temperature value
    temp_value = int(parts[1])
    
    print("Temperature monitoring received:", raw_data)
    
    # Check if temperature threshold is exceeded
    if temp_value > 200:
        print('WARNING: Temperature critical - exceeds 200 degrees')
        
        # Format alert message
        alert_msg = f"{parts[0]} {temp_value}"
        kafka_client.send(target_topic, alert_msg.encode('utf-8'))
        kafka_client.flush()
        
        # Rate limiting between alerts
        time.sleep(5)

def fetch_google_calendar_auth():
    # Locate the client secrets file
    secrets_file = 'client_secret.json'

        print("Error: client_secret.json missing in current directory.")
        return
    
    # Set required permissions (read-only calendar access)

    oauth_flow = InstalledAppFlow.from_client_secrets_file(secrets_file, scopes_list)

    # Attempt to load existing credentials
    creds = None
    if os.path.exists(token_file):

    # Refresh or obtain new credentials if needed
    if not creds or not creds.valid:

            'token_endpoint': creds.token_uri,

# Extract latitude and longitude coordinates from a KML file containing a single path
def kml_to_coordinates(input_file):
    """Parse KML file and return list of (longitude, latitude) tuples"""
    from fastkml import kml, geometry
    with open(input_file, 'rt') as file:
        content = file.read()
    kml_object = kml.KML()
    kml_object.from_string(content)
    document_features = list(kml_object.features())
    placemark_features = list(document_features[0].features())
    coord_list = list(placemark_features[0].geometry.coords)
    latlon_pairs = [(lon, lat) for lon, lat, _ in coord_list]
    return latlon_pairs

def reverse_words(text: str) -> str:
    """
    Converts the input text into reversed-word order (Yoda-style).
    Args:
    text (str): The original text to be transformed.
    Returns:
    str: Text with words in reverse order.
    """
    word_list = text.split()
    yoda_style = " ".join(word_list[::-1])
    return yoda_style

    """
    Applies Yoda-style transformation to each string in a list.
    Args:
    text_array (List[str]): List of input strings to transform.
    Returns:
    List[str]: List of transformed strings with reversed word order.
    """
    transformed_list = [reverse_words(text) for text in text_array]
    return transformed_list

# Check if a file has executable permissions 
import os
import stat

def check_file_executable(path):
    # Define executable permission bits for user, group, and others
    exec_perms = stat.S_IXUSR | stat.S_IXGRP | stat.S_IXOTH
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        return False
    file_stat = os.stat(path)
    file_mode = file_stat.st_mode
    if file_mode & exec_perms:
        return True
    return False

import numpy as np

def interpolate_data(data_values, target_count):
    """
    Apply linear interpolation to the provided data sequence.
    
    Parameters
    ----------
    data_values : list or numpy.ndarray
        The original data points for interpolation.
    target_count : int
        The desired number of interpolated points across the data range.
        
    Returns
    -------
    result_array : numpy.ndarray
        Array containing the interpolated values.
        
    Examples
    --------
    >>> interpolate_data([1, 2, 3, 4], 5)
    array([1.  , 1.75, 2.5 , 3.25, 4.  ])
    >>> interpolate_data([10, 20, 30, 40, 50], 3)
    array([10., 30., 50.])
    """
    data_values = np.array(data_values)
    original_indices = np.arange(len(data_values))
    new_indices = np.linspace(0, len(data_values) - 1, target_count)
    result_array = np.interp(new_indices, original_indices, data_values)
    return result_array

from scapy.all import wrpcap, Ether, IP, TCP

def extract_and_store_packets(start_timestamp, end_timestamp, incoming_data, filename):
    # Filter packets within the specified time range
    selected_packets = [pkt for pkt in incoming_data if start_timestamp <= pkt['timestamp'] <= end_timestamp]
    
    # Construct new packets with Ethernet, IP, and TCP headers
    prepared_packets = [
        Ether() / IP() / TCP(dport=80, sport=1025) / pkt['payload']

    ]
    
    # Write the filtered packets to the output file
    wrpcap(filename, prepared_packets)

    existing_record = db_session.get(model_class, record_id)
    if not existing_record:

    # Prepare updated fields excluding unset values

        output["JetSelection"] = jet_selection_pattern.group(1)
    
    # Extract jetId value
    jet_id_pattern = re.search(r"jetId\s*=\s*\"(.*?)\"", config_string)
    if jet_id_pattern:
        output["JetId"] = jet_id_pattern.group(1)
    
    # Extract njets value as integer
    num_jets_pattern = re.search(r"njets\s*=\s*(\d+)", config_string)
    if num_jets_pattern:
        output["NumJets"] = int(num_jets_pattern.group(1))

# Build a binary similarity matrix based on keyword relevance scores
def build_keyword_similarity(relevance_data, threshold_value=0.2):
    """
    Creates a binary similarity matrix from relevance data where entries above the threshold are marked as similar
    
    Args:
    relevance_data: 2D list containing relevance scores between keywords
    threshold_value: Minimum score required to consider two keywords as similar (default is 0.2)
    Returns:
    similarity_matrix: 2D list with 1s for similar pairs and 0s otherwise
    """
    similarity_matrix = []
    num_items = len(relevance_data)
    
    for row_idx in range(num_items):
        current_row = []
        for col_idx in range(num_items):
            if relevance_data[row_idx][col_idx] >= threshold_value:
                current_row.append(1)  # Keywords are considered similar
            else:
                current_row.append(0)  # Keywords are not similar
        similarity_matrix.append(current_row)
    
    return similarity_matrix

import urllib.parse

def build_url_from_params(params_dict, key_mapping_dict):
    """
    Transform a dictionary of parameters into a URL-encoded query string.
    :param params_dict: dictionary containing parameter values
    :param key_mapping_dict: dictionary mapping parameter names to query parameter names
    :return: URL-encoded query string
    """
    encoded_pairs = dict()
    for param_key in key_mapping_dict.keys():
        param_value = params_dict.get(param_key)
        if param_value is not None:
            encoded_pairs[key_mapping_dict[param_key]] = str(param_value)
    return urllib.parse.urlencode(encoded_pairs)

# Proxy server implementation using asyncio
import asyncio

async def process_client(reader, writer):
    remote_address = '192.168.1.100'
    remote_port = 443
    try:
        remote_reader, remote_writer = await asyncio.open_connection(remote_address, remote_port)
        while True:
            chunk = await reader.read(2048)
            if not chunk:
                break
            remote_writer.write(chunk)
            await remote_writer.drain()
    except ConnectionResetError:
        print('Connection was reset by peer')
    finally:
        writer.close()
        await writer.wait_closed()

async def run_server():
    proxy_server = await asyncio.start_server(
        process_client, '0.0.0.0', 9000)
    async with proxy_server:
        await proxy_server.serve_forever()

asyncio.run(run_server())

# Fetch data from a database table using SQLAlchemy
from sqlalchemy import create_engine, MetaData, Table
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker
from sqlalchemy.sql import select

DB_CONNECTION_STRING = "postgresql://username:password@localhost/database_name"

def fetch_records_from_table(table_identifier):
    db_engine = create_engine(DB_CONNECTION_STRING)
    SessionClass = sessionmaker(bind=db_engine)
    active_session = SessionClass()
    
    db_metadata = MetaData()
    target_table = Table(table_identifier, db_metadata, autoload_with=db_engine)
    
    sql_query = select([target_table])
    query_result = active_session.execute(sql_query).fetchall()
    
    records_list = [
        {col_name: row_value for col_name, row_value in zip(query_result.keys(), row)}
        for row in query_result
    ]
    
    active_session.close()
    return records_list

def execute_step(state):
    """Add element to a mutable sequence.

    state['data']: A mutable sequence to which the element will be added.
    state['value']: The element to be added to the sequence.
    """
    if not isinstance(state['data'], (list, bytearray, memoryview)):
        raise TypeError("Input sequence must be a mutable sequence")
    state['data'].append(state['value'])

# Task manager implementation for handling service lifecycle
import asyncio

class Worker:
    async def execute(self):
        pass
    async def shutdown(self):
        pass

class Coordinator:
    def __init__(self, worker: Worker):
        self.worker = worker
        self.__shutdown_flag = False
    
    async def start(self):
        while not self.__shutdown_flag:
            await self.worker.execute()
            await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
    
    async def terminate(self):
        self.__shutdown_flag = True
        await self.worker.shutdown()

# Function to compute the largest number with all lower bits set
def max_bitmask(value):
    value = value | (value >> 1)
    value = value | (value >> 2)
    value = value | (value >> 4)
    value = value | (value >> 8)
    return value

import numpy as np
class CosineDistance(AbstractDistance):
    """
        Negated Mahalanobis Cosine Distance.
    
        Literature:
            "Studies on sensitivity of face recognition performance to eye location accuracy.". Master Thesis (2004), Wang
    """
    def __init__(self, mahalanobis_matrix):
        AbstractDistance.__init__(self, "CosineDistance")
        self.mahalanobis_matrix = mahalanobis_matrix
        
    def calculate_distance(self, vector_a, vector_b):
        """
        Calculate the Negated Mahalanobis Cosine Distance between two input vectors vector_a and vector_b.
        Args:
        vector_a (array-like): First input vector
        vector_b (array-like): Second input vector
        Returns:
        float: Negated Mahalanobis Cosine Distance between vectors vector_a and vector_b
        """
        vec_a = np.asarray(vector_a).flatten()
        vec_b = np.asarray(vector_b).flatten()
        
        diff_vector = vec_a - vec_b
        mahalanobis_term = np.dot(np.dot(diff_vector, self.mahalanobis_matrix), diff_vector)
        
        norm_a = np.linalg.norm(vec_a)
        norm_b = np.linalg.norm(vec_b)
        
        distance = -mahalanobis_term / (norm_a * norm_b)
        return distance

import re
from typing import List, Dict

def extract_card_info(text: str) -> List[Dict[str, str]]:
    output = []
    
    # Pattern for standard card format with version fields
    pattern1 = re.compile(
        r"1\s+(?P<shelf_id>\d+)\s+(?P<slot_id>\d+)\s+"
        r"(?P<config_type>\S+)\s+(?P<real_type>\S+|)\s+(?P<port_num>\d+)\s+"
        r"(?P<hardware_version>V?\S+|)\s+(?P<software_version>V\S+|)\s+(?P<operational_status>INSERVICE|OFFLINE|STANDBY|NOPOWER)"
    )
    
    # Pattern for alternate card format (without software version)
    pattern2 = re.compile(
        r"(?P<shelf_id>\d+)\s+(?P<slot_id>\d+)\s+"
        r"(?P<config_type>\S+)\s+(?P<real_type>\S+|)\s+(?P<port_num>\d+)\s+"
        r"(?P<hardware_version>V?\S+|N/A|)\s+(?P<operational_status>INSERVICE|OFFLINE|STANDBY|NOPOWER)"
    )
    
    for record in text.split('\n'):
        match1 = pattern1.match(record)
        match2 = pattern2.match(record)
        
        if match1:
            output.append(match1.groupdict())
        elif match2:
            output.append(match2.groupdict())
            
    return output

# Create a quantum circuit for multi-controlled Toffoli gate
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit, QuantumRegister, ClassicalRegister
from qiskit.circuit.library import MCMT

def build_mct_circuit(control_count):
    # Define quantum registers for control and target qubits
    controls = QuantumRegister(control_count, name='ctrl')
    target = QuantumRegister(1, name='tgt')
    
    # Create classical register for measurement outcomes
    classical_reg = ClassicalRegister(control_count, name='meas')
    
    # Initialize the quantum circuit
    qc = QuantumCircuit(controls, target, classical_reg)
    
    # Add the MCT operation
    qc.append(MCMT(control_count, 'cx', ctrl_qubits=controls, tgt_qubit=target, use_basis_gates=True), controls[:] + target[:])
    
    return qc

from scaaml.aes_forward import AESSBOX

# Import required Keras modules for model construction
import keras
from keras.models import Model
from keras.layers import Dropout, Dense, Concatenate
from keras.initializers import RandomNormal

def build_classifier_model(pretrained_model, input_features):
    # Apply dropout regularization to each feature tensor
    dropout_outputs = [Dropout(0.5)(feature) for feature in input_features]
    
    # Create dense layers with ReLU activation and specified kernel initialization
    hidden_layers = [
        Dense(2, activation='relu', kernel_initializer=RandomNormal(mean=0.0, stddev=0.001))(dropout)
        for dropout in dropout_outputs
    ]
    
    # Combine all hidden layer outputs along axis 1
    merged_output = Concatenate(axis=1)(hidden_layers)
    
    # Add final classification layer with softmax activation
    classification_output = Dense(2, activation='softmax', 
                                  kernel_initializer=RandomNormal(mean=0.0, stddev=0.001))(merged_output)
    
    # Construct the complete model using pretrained base input and final output
    classifier_model = Model(inputs=pretrained_model.input, outputs=classification_output)
    return classifier_model

    Processes the file specified by the path_input.
    
    Args:
    path_input: A string representing the file path.
    
    Returns:
    Path: The path to the existing file if it already exists, otherwise None.
    """
    path_input = Path(path_input)
    if not path_input.exists():
        try:
            # create parent directories
            path_input.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            path_input.touch()  # create the file itself
        except Exception:
            return None
        path_input.unlink()  # delete it
    return path_input

# Custom loss function combining MSE and L2 regularization
import torch
from torch.autograd import Variable

def custom_loss(predictions, targets):
    # Compute mean squared error between predictions and targets
    mse = torch.mean((predictions - targets) ** 2)
    # Compute L2 norm (Euclidean norm) of the predictions tensor
    l2_penalty = torch.norm(predictions, p=2)
    # Combine both components into final loss value
    total_loss = mse + l2_penalty
    return total_loss

# Custom file reader with progress tracking
from typing import Optional
from overrides import overrides
from pathlib import Path
from tqdm import tqdm

class TextFileProcessor:
    def __init__(self, filepath: str):
        self.filepath = Path(filepath)
        self._bar = None
    
    def get_file_size(self) -> int:
        return self.filepath.stat().st_size
    
    @overrides
    def load(self, limit: Optional[int] = -1) -> str:
        if self._bar is not None:
            self._bar.close()
        
        self._bar = tqdm(total=self.get_file_size(), desc="Loading", unit="B", unit_scale=True)
        output = ""
        
        with open(self.filepath, 'r') as source_file:
            if limit == -1:
                output = source_file.read()
                self._bar.update(self.get_file_size() - self._bar.n)
            else:
                fragment = source_file.read(limit)
                while fragment:
                    output += fragment
                    self._bar.update(len(fragment))
                    fragment = source_file.read(limit)
        
        self._bar.close()
        return output

# Perform FFT-based convolution of image with kernel
import numpy as np
import warnings

def fft_convolve(image, filter_kernel):
    try:
        import pyfftw
        fft_func = pyfftw.interfaces.numpy_fft.fftn
        ifft_func = pyfftw.interfaces.numpy_fft.ifftn
    except ImportError:
        warnings.warn("pyfftw not available. Falling back to numpy.fft.")
        fft_func = np.fft.fftn
        ifft_func = np.fft.ifftn
    
    image_freq = fft_func(image)
    kernel_freq = fft_func(filter_kernel, s=image.shape)
    result_freq = image_freq * kernel_freq
    result_spatial = ifft_func(result_freq)
    result_abs = np.abs(result_spatial)
    return result_abs

# Represents a polygon in 2D space
class Polygon:
    """
    A polygon is a two-dimensional figure defined by a sequence of
    a minimum of three ordered and non-coincident vertices
    connected to form a closed polygonal chain.
    """
    def compute_surface_area(self):
        vertex_count = len(self.vertices)
        result = 0
        for index in range(vertex_count):
            next_index = (index + 1) % vertex_count
            result += self.vertices[index].x * self.vertices[next_index].y
            result -= self.vertices[next_index].x * self.vertices[index].y
        result = abs(result) / 2
        return result

from gplearn.genetic import SymbolicRegressor
from sklearn.model_selection import GridSearchCV

def fit_symbolic_regression(x_data, y_data):
    # Define hyperparameter search space
    hyperparams = {
        'population_size': [1000, 5000, 10000],
        'generations': [10, 20, 50],
        'stopping_criteria': [0.9, 0.95, 0.99],
        'store': [True, False],
        'p_mutate': [0.1, 0.2, 0.3],
        'p_crossover': [0.3, 0.5, 0.7],
        'select_method': ["random", "tournament"]
    }
    
    # Initialize the base estimator with default generations and fixed random state
    estimator = SymbolicRegressor(generations=10, random_state=42)
    
    # Set up grid search with cross-validation
    cv_search = GridSearchCV(estimator, hyperparams, cv=5, scoring='neg_mean_squared_error')
    
    # Fit the grid search to the data
    cv_search.fit(x_data, y_data)
    
    # Extract best model and corresponding hyperparameters
    optimal_model = cv_search.best_estimator_
    optimal_params = cv_search.best_params_
    
    return optimal_model, optimal_params

def compute_event_length(event_data: dict) -> int:

    finish_timestamp = event_data.get("end_time")

# A* pathfinding implementation for maze solving
import heapq

def solve_maze():
    initial_pos = maze_map.get_start()
    goal_pos = maze_map.get_end()
    
    priority_queue = [(0, initial_pos, [])]  # (f_score, (x, y), current_path)
    visited_nodes = set()
    
    while priority_queue:
        _, (current_x, current_y), current_path = heapq.heappop(priority_queue)
        
        if (current_x, current_y) == goal_pos:
            return current_path + [(current_x, current_y)]
        
        if (current_x, current_y) in visited_nodes:
            continue
        
        visited_nodes.add((current_x, current_y))
        
        for delta_x, delta_y in [(1, 0), (-1, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1)]:
            next_x, next_y = current_x + delta_x, current_y + delta_y
            if maze_map.is_valid(next_x, next_y):
                updated_path = current_path + [(current_x, current_y)]
                g_cost = len(updated_path)
                h_cost = maze_map.heuristic(next_x, next_y)
                f_cost = g_cost + h_cost
                heapq.heappush(priority_queue, (f_cost, (next_x, next_y), updated_path))
    
    return []  # No valid path exists

import BaseHTTPServer
import SimpleHTTPServer
import ssl
import sys
import logging
from datetime import datetime

class CustomHandler(SimpleHTTPServer.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler):
    def log_request(self, code='-', size='-'):
        entry = '{} - - [{}] "{} {}"'.format(self.client_address[0], self.log_date_time_string(), self.command, self.path)
        self.write_log(entry)
    
    def write_log(self, entry):
        with open(self.server.base_dir + "/access.log", "a") as log_file:
            log_file.write(entry + "\n")

class SecureServer:
    def __init__(self, base_directory):
        self.base_dir = base_directory
    
    def start_servers(self, http_port, https_port, private_key, cert_file):
        # HTTP server instance
        http_server = BaseHTTPServer.HTTPServer(('', http_port), SimpleHTTPServer.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler)
        http_server.base_dir = self.base_dir
        
        # HTTPS server instance
        https_server = BaseHTTPServer.HTTPServer(('', https_port), CustomHandler)
        https_server.base_dir = self.base_dir
        https_server.socket = ssl.wrap_socket(https_server.socket, server_side=True, keyfile=private_key, certfile=cert_file)
        
        try:
            logging.basicConfig(filename=self.base_dir + "/error.log", level=logging.ERROR)
            http_server.serve_forever()
            https_server.serve_forever()
        except Exception as error:
            logging.error("Server issue: {}".format(str(error)))

import random

def select_from_groups(group_data_dict, max_count=None):
    selected_elements = []
    groups = list(group_data_dict.values())
    group_counts = [(group_id, len(group)) for group_id, group in group_data_dict.items()]
    group_counts.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
    
    while max_count is None or len(selected_elements) < max_count:
        for group_id, _ in group_counts:
            if max_count is not None and len(selected_elements) >= max_count:
                break
            group = group_data_dict[group_id]
            if not group:
                continue
            element = random.choice(group)
            selected_elements.append(element)
            group.remove(element)
    
    return selected_elements[:max_count] if max_count is not None else selected_elements

# Database cache management module using SQLAlchemy
from sqlalchemy import create_engine, MetaData, Table, Column, BigInteger, Unicode, DateTime
from sqlalchemy.sql import select, insert, update, delete

class DataCacheHandler:
    def __init__(self, database_url):
        self.db_engine = create_engine(database_url)
        self.metadata_obj = MetaData(bind=self.db_engine)
        self.storage_table = Table('cache', self.metadata_obj,
                                   Column('id', BigInteger, nullable=False),
                                   Column('identifier', Unicode, nullable=True),
                                   Column('data', Unicode, nullable=True),
                                   Column('timestamp', DateTime, nullable=True))
    
    def add_entry(self, identifier, data):
        with self.db_engine.connect() as connection:
            stmt = insert(self.storage_table).values(identifier=identifier, data=data)
            stmt = stmt.on_conflict_do_update(index_elements=['identifier'], set_=dict(data=stmt.excluded.data))
            connection.execute(stmt)
    
    def fetch_entry(self, identifier):
        with self.db_engine.connect() as connection:
            query = select([self.storage_table.c.data]).where(self.storage_table.c.identifier == identifier)
            output = connection.execute(query).scalar()
            return output if output is not None else "Entry missing"
    
    def modify_entry(self, identifier, data):
        with self.db_engine.connect() as connection:
            modify_stmt = update(self.storage_table).where(self.storage_table.c.identifier == identifier).values(data=data)
            modify_stmt = modify_stmt.on_conflict_do_update(index_elements=['identifier'], set_=dict(data=modify_stmt.excluded.data))
            connection.execute(modify_stmt)
    
    def remove_entry(self, identifier):
        with self.db_engine.connect() as connection:
            removal_stmt = delete(self.storage_table).where(self.storage_table.c.identifier == identifier)
            connection.execute(removal_stmt)

# Compute Intersection over Union (IoU) between two sets of bounding boxes
import torch

def compute_iou(boxes1, boxes2):
    num_boxes1, num_boxes2 = boxes1.shape[0], boxes2.shape[0]
    iou_matrix = torch.zeros((num_boxes1, num_boxes2))
    
    # Handle empty case
    if num_boxes1 * num_boxes2 == 0:
        return iou_matrix
    
    swapped = False
    if boxes1.shape[0] > boxes2.shape[0]:
        boxes1, boxes2 = boxes2, boxes1
        iou_matrix = torch.zeros((num_boxes2, num_boxes1))
        swapped = True
    
    # Compute intersection coordinates
    x_top_left = torch.max(boxes1[:, 0].unsqueeze(1), boxes2[:, 0].unsqueeze(0))
    y_top_left = torch.max(boxes1[:, 1].unsqueeze(1), boxes2[:, 1].unsqueeze(0))
    x_bottom_right = torch.min(boxes1[:, 2].unsqueeze(1), boxes2[:, 2].unsqueeze(0))
    y_bottom_right = torch.min(boxes1[:, 3].unsqueeze(1), boxes2[:, 3].unsqueeze(0))
    
    # Compute intersection area
    width = torch.clamp(x_bottom_right - x_top_left, min=0)
    height = torch.clamp(y_bottom_right - y_top_left, min=0)
    intersection = width * height
    
    # Compute individual box areas
    area_boxes1 = (boxes1[:, 2] - boxes1[:, 0]) * (boxes1[:, 3] - boxes1[:, 1])
    area_boxes2 = (boxes2[:, 2] - boxes2[:, 0]) * (boxes2[:, 3] - boxes2[:, 1])
    
    # Compute union area
    union = area_boxes1.unsqueeze(1) + area_boxes2.unsqueeze(0) - intersection
    
    # Compute IoU
    iou_result = intersection / union
    
    # Return in original order if boxes were swapped
    if swapped:
        return iou_result.T
    else:
        return iou_result

from math import floor

def convert_gps_to_dms(coord_value):
    decimal_degrees = float(coord_value)
    deg = floor(decimal_degrees)
    min_float = (decimal_degrees - deg) * 60
    mins = floor(min_float)

    return (deg, mins, secs)

# Parse a snowflake ID into its components 
import datetime

def decode_snowflake(snowflake_id: int) -> dict:
    # Validate input
    if not isinstance(snowflake_id, int) or snowflake_id < 0 or snowflake_id > 9223372036854775807:
        raise ValueError("Invalid snowflake ID provided.")
    
    # Extract timestamp with custom epoch (January 1, 2021)
    epoch_offset = 1609459200000
    timestamp_ms = (snowflake_id >> 22) + epoch_offset
    formatted_time = datetime.datetime.utcfromtimestamp(timestamp_ms / 1000).strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f')
    
    # Extract worker and sequence numbers
    worker_identifier = (snowflake_id >> 12) & 0x3FF
    sequence_value = snowflake_id & 0xFFF
    
    return {
        "timestamp": formatted_time,
        "worker_id": worker_identifier,
        "sequence_number": sequence_value
    }

# Find all valid split points in a construction sequence
def find_split_points(sequence, first=None, last=None):
    """
    Generate all possible split positions between first and last indices.
    The first and last positions themselves are excluded from the result.
    """
    first = first if first is not None else 0
    last = last if last is not None else len(sequence)
    split_positions = []
    previous = first - 1  # Set previous to one position before the starting index
    for j in range(first, last - 1):
        if j - previous > 1:  # Ensure there's at least one element between previous and j
            split_positions.append(j)  # Record the valid split position
        previous = j  # Update previous to current position
    return split_positions

# Linear regression using JAX JIT compilation
import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp

@jax.jit
def _linear_regression(x_vals, y_vals):
    count = len(x_vals)
    total_x = jnp.sum(x_vals)
    total_y = jnp.sum(y_vals)
    total_product = jnp.sum(x_vals * y_vals)
    total_x_sq = jnp.sum(x_vals ** 2)
    
    slope = (count * total_product - total_x * total_y) / (count * total_x_sq - total_x ** 2)
    intercept = (total_y - slope * total_x) / count
    
    return slope, intercept
